purpose: The field catalogue an export profile (policy/exports/<name>.yaml, lane 01) may reference by name. One entry per promoted field, plus steward edits and the ADR-0041 provenance rung. `served_by` is the load-bearing column: a field with `served_by: null` is produced by doc-tools but is NOT reachable on the extraction route, so no profile can emit it today without lane 01 widening the route.

seal.producer_leg: Every `producer.field` is checked against what the code actually emits: the BAML class property sets in doc_tools/baml_client/type_builder.py and the field_path/key sets written by doc_tools.utils.sustainment_merge.build_review_items.
seal.contract_leg: Every `wire` entry is checked against tests/fixtures/cortex_bff_extraction_pin.json, an extract of invincible-agent:docs/api/cortex-bff.openapi.json pinned at a named sha.
seal.stricter_than_the_pin: ARCHITECT RULING 2026-10-28 (relayed in cortex-ui's packet of the same day): a ref without `bbox` is not legal; the shape is {page, bbox, note?}. It stays nullable -- null means 'on this page, no box' (ruling 205) -- but the key is always PRESENT, reversing the earlier 205 note that omitting it was the same as null. The pinned extract still reads required: [page] because lane 01 had not regenerated the doc when the pin was taken, so the seal asserts the floor {page, bbox} itself rather than deriving it from the pin. Both of our emitters already satisfy it, measured: sustainment_merge._row_wire_evidence_ref initialises bbox to None, and leaf_read.wire_evidence_ref always writes the key. Nothing in the producer changes.
seal.NOT_sealed: That the pinned extract is still what the platform serves. The extract is a frozen copy; a platform-side change does not red this repo until the pin is re-taken. That freshness leg is #181's mechanism (tests/pins/invincible-agent.ref) and #181 is still a draft. Two green legs are not a covered span -- name the hop that is open.

field_scopes.notice: One value per notice. A per-notice profile emits one row of these; a per-(notice,part) profile repeats them on every row.
field_scopes.row: One value per (notice, part, field). The extraction route serves ONLY the parts[i].* review items as rows, in review.json file order.
field_scopes.steward_edit: A correction a steward made during promotion. Not an extracted value.
field_scopes.provenance: ADR-0041 trust rung, written at ingest. NOT the row-level match method -- see collisions.

collisions.name: mfr_source
collisions.detail: Two unrelated fields share the name. The PRODUCER's header.mfr_source is a verbatim source substring (BAML: 'Verbatim source substring for mfr - MANDATORY whenever mfr is non-null'), one of a family with pub_date_source / mfr_parent_source / doc_level_ltb_date_source. The CONTRACT's notice.mfr_source is a closed enum {header, identity} naming which arm produced the value. A profile that writes `mfr_source` must say which it means; this catalogue names them `header.mfr_source` and `notice.mfr_source`.

collisions.name: obtained_via
collisions.detail: On the extraction wire, row.obtained_via is the MATCH METHOD (the producer's match_method: unique / region_preferred / ambiguous / not_found / text_layer_cell / text_layer_word / inherited_doc_level / derived). In ADR-0041, obtained_via is the TRUST RUNG (None or 'user-drop', with siblings authoritative_source and standing). The packet's phrase 'provenance rung' means the ADR-0041 one. Cataloguing row.obtained_via as the rung would export match methods under a provenance heading.

collisions.name: scope
collisions.detail: RESOLVED IN THIS CATALOGUE 2026-10-30: the per-field key is now `field_scope` and the vocabulary block is `field_scopes`. Lane 01 answered the question on 2026-10-30 -- 'yes. No iagent code reads the catalogue yet, so the rename costs nothing here, and it keeps the key from being read as an OAuth scope. Rename it before anything consumes it' -- and this change lands WITH that first consumer, doc_tools/batch/profile.py, so no consumer ever read the old key. THE COLLISION ITSELF IS NOT RESOLVED, only our side of it. It was three meanings, two of them sharing the SAME TOKENS. (1) Here, the FIELD scope: notice / row / steward_edit / provenance -- which scope a field belongs to; now spelled `field_scope`. (2) cortex-ui's proposed profile-listing route (packet 2026-10-28, 'what cortex needs on the wire', route 1) returns [{name, format, scope, label?}] where `scope` is 'row'|'notice' meaning the ROW GRANULARITY of the export. (3) lane fin's CDRL profile header (packet 2026-10-28) uses the same key with the value 'program'. Meanings (2) and (3) still disagree with each other, and that is lane 01's to settle in policy/exports/. On our own profile header the granularity key is `granularity`, never `scope` -- docs/contracts/batch-column-map.md section 2 -- so a doc-tools profile and this catalogue no longer share a token with either.

unverified_mappings: notice.notice_date <- header.pub_date. The contract declares notice_date with no type and no description, and nothing in doc-tools writes a field of that name. The mapping is lane 01's and is NOT asserted here.

notice.mfr_source <- (unknown). The enum values {header, identity} name doc-tools' two header arms, but no doc-tools field carries those values; header.mfr_source carries a substring. Lane 01 derives this somewhere on their side.
not_extracted: change_type -- named by the batch-fixture ruling (closed vocabulary, free text to change_type_note). Measured absent: zero occurrences in doc_tools/utils/sustainment_merge.py and doc_tools/plugins/sustainment.py. Not a promoted field, so no profile can reference it.
effective_date -- same ruling, same measurement. Not a promoted field.

A batch column-map vocabulary. SUPERSEDED 2026-10-29: it is now written, at docs/contracts/batch-column-map.md (contract_version 1), after the architect ruled the vocabulary 7f's to write and lane 01's to review. It remains correct that `column_map` / `column-map` has zero occurrences in doc_tools/, registry/ and docs/ OUTSIDE that contract -- it is a contract with no implementation, so nothing here is reachable from a profile yet. Two of the four batch-fixture rulings name fields this catalogue records as not extracted at all: `change_type` and `effective_date`, immediately above, which that contract declares a hard stop at profile-validation time rather than working around.

fields.name: notice.ingest_id
fields.notes: The ingest key, not a document field. Its shape is no SDK contract -- do not parse it.

fields.name: notice.notice_id
fields.notes: Can be a path fragment, or a filename-derived string when the header call timed out. Not a stable key.

fields.name: notice.content_kind
fields.notes: Platform-owned: what a kind IS is theirs, what doc-tools RUNS is ours.

fields.name: notice.leaf
fields.notes: Read from the ROW only (_row_leaf). A row with no leaf shows leaf: null whatever review.json says.

fields.name: notice.corrected_by
fields.notes: Who corrected the leaf, if anyone.

fields.name: notice.part_count
fields.notes: Counts parts, not rows. A notice with zero parts still gets its notice node.

fields.name: notice.rows_without_evidence
fields.notes: Counted by the route: a row with no usable page/bbox carries evidence_ref: null. Derived, not extracted.

fields.name: notice.review_ref
fields.notes: Stays the ORIGINAL key after a rejection; relocated_to says where the objects went.

fields.name: notice.relocated_to
fields.notes: Set for a REJECTED row, whose evidence moved to rejected/<id>/. A rejection strands every ref filed against the original location.

fields.name: notice.mfr
fields.notes: LLM-extracted, so unconstrained. review.json carries a header.mfr review item WITH a wire_evidence_ref, but the Notice object has no evidence_ref field, so the header's evidence is unreachable on this route.

fields.name: notice.mfr_parent
fields.notes: Same evidence gap as notice.mfr.

fields.name: notice.mfr_source
fields.notes: COLLISION: not the producer's header.mfr_source. This says which arm produced mfr, not what substring it was read from. Mapping unverified.

fields.name: notice.notice_date
fields.notes: Mapping to header.pub_date is UNVERIFIED -- the contract gives it no type and no description, and no doc-tools field carries this name. A date transform in a profile needs the format settled first, and pub_date is a PRINT STAMP, not an effective date.

fields.name: header.doc_id
fields.notes: Served as notice.notice_id, so reachable under that name only.

fields.name: header.doc_type
fields.notes: Produced, not served. Not the same thing as notice.leaf.

fields.name: header.revision
fields.notes: Produced, not served.

fields.name: header.pub_date
fields.notes: Carries a header-region review item WITH a wire_evidence_ref, none of which is served. A PRINT STAMP: agreement on pub_date is agreement on when the sheet was printed, not on when anything takes effect.

fields.name: header.pub_date_source
fields.notes: Verbatim source substring, fed to the review item source_snippet.

fields.name: header.mfr_source
fields.notes: COLLISION: a verbatim source substring, NOT the contract {header, identity} enum. Measured set to None by sustainment_header_trust.py on at least two paths, despite BAML calling it mandatory whenever mfr is non-null.

fields.name: header.mfr_parent_source
fields.notes: Verbatim source substring.

fields.name: header.categories
fields.notes: A DERIVED review item: region 'derived', so it carries NO wire_evidence_ref by ruling. A list, so emitting it to csv needs a join transform the mapping language does not have yet.

fields.name: header.summary
fields.notes: DERIVED: region 'derived', no wire_evidence_ref by ruling. Free prose -- unsafe in a fixed-width csv column.

fields.name: header.doc_level_ltb_date
fields.notes: Produced with a header-region review item and evidence, and NOT served on this route. It is the value that unsourced part-level LTB rows INHERIT, so a per-part export omitting it loses the only source those dates have.

fields.name: header.doc_level_ltb_date_source
fields.notes: Verbatim source substring.

fields.name: row.row_index
fields.notes: Position in review.json file order.

fields.name: row.part_index
fields.notes: The grouping key for one-row-per-(notice,part). Up to three field rows share one part_index.

fields.name: row.mpn
fields.notes: The row part identity, repeated on all of that part field rows. An OCR ditto quote in an MPN has returned a 400 on a whole graph insert -- do not assume it is clean enough to key on.

fields.name: row.field

vocabulary.schema_note: The CONTRACT declares a bare string with no enum; the PRODUCER emits only these four on this route. Closed in practice, open in the schema -- a profile keying on it should tolerate an unknown value.

fields.notes: Renamed from the producer field_path. This is the discriminator a column list uses to pick which value a column takes.

fields.name: row.extracted_value
fields.notes: Renamed from the producer `value`. A null is EXCLUDED from corpus scoring, and a ruled None is indistinguishable from a missing one -- so a null here does not mean the field was absent from the document.

fields.name: row.obtained_via

vocabulary.schema_note: Two families: four from provenance.resolve_value, four set directly by the merge. The schema declares no enum, so this list is measured, not guaranteed.

fields.notes: COLLISION: this is the MATCH METHOD, not the ADR-0041 provenance rung. `inherited_doc_level` means the value came from header.doc_level_ltb_date, not from the part own row.

fields.name: row.match_confidence
fields.notes: Defaults to 0.0 when provenance carries none. Confidence in the LOCATION of the value, not in the value.

fields.name: row.needs_review
fields.notes: Hardcoded False on the parts[i].ltb_date path, so a false here is not a statement about that field.

fields.name: row.review_reason

values: affected_mpn not found verbatim in OCR text (possible hallucination)

fields.notes: Free text; the two measured wordings are listed.

fields.name: row.source_snippet
fields.notes: The verbatim substring the model says it read the value from: affected_mpn_source / replacement_mpn_source / customer_mpn_source / ltb_date_source, by row. This is where the *_source family DOES reach the wire.

fields.name: part.affected_mpn
fields.notes: A profile names this field; the value is row.extracted_value on the row whose row.field is 'parts[i].affected_mpn', and its verbatim substring is row.source_snippet on that same row. One wire column carries all three part values, so the column list needs the selector, not just a name. Distinct from row.mpn: row.mpn is the part identity repeated on every row of the part, this is the extracted value of the one affected_mpn row. Carries review_reason 'affected_mpn not found verbatim in OCR text (possible hallucination)' when the value is not in the OCR text.

fields.name: part.replacement_mpn
fields.notes: A profile names this field; the value is row.extracted_value on the row whose row.field is 'parts[i].replacement_mpn', and its verbatim substring is row.source_snippet on that same row. One wire column carries all three part values, so the column list needs the selector, not just a name. The row is emitted ONLY when the part has a replacement_mpn, so a part with none has two rows, not three -- a per-part profile must tolerate the absent row rather than expect a null. The corpus scorer has no replacement arm, so this field is unscored.

fields.name: part.customer_mpn
fields.notes: The CUSTOMER's own part number for the row's affected part: an alias of affected_mpn, NOT a replacement and NOT a second affected part. A profile names this field; the value is row.extracted_value on the row whose row.field is 'parts[i].customer_mpn', and its verbatim substring is row.source_snippet on that same row. The row is emitted ONLY when the part has a customer_mpn, so a part with none simply lacks the row rather than carrying a null. A customer cell may legitimately hold two ids for one affected part (carried verbatim, not split). Row field and review surface ONLY: it is never written to the graph, because component IRIs are shared across notices and a wrongly written alias cannot be withdrawn. The corpus scorer has no customer arm, so this field is unscored.

fields.name: part.ltb_date
fields.notes: A profile names this field; the value is row.extracted_value on the row whose row.field is 'parts[i].ltb_date', and its verbatim substring is row.source_snippet on that same row. One wire column carries all three part values, so the column list needs the selector, not just a name. Emitted only when the part has an ltb_date. needs_review is hardcoded False on this path. Where the part had no date of its own the value is INHERITED from header.doc_level_ltb_date, flagged on the wire as obtained_via 'inherited_doc_level' -- so an export column of part LTB dates silently mixes row-level and doc-level facts unless it also carries obtained_via. No date format is guaranteed: the ISO-8601 normalisation the batch ruling calls for is not built.

fields.name: row.evidence_ref
fields.notes: Served AS IS since invincible-agent ac77ef61. Keys are exactly {page, bbox, note?}: additionalProperties is false and nothing else is served -- no bboxes, page_dims, units or quality. ABSENT (not null) on the producer side when the field is derived or has no page; the route turns that into evidence_ref: null and counts it in rows_without_evidence.

fields.name: row.evidence_ref.page
fields.notes: 1-based (enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1)); the schema sets minimum 1. The ONLY required key of EvidenceRef.

fields.name: row.evidence_ref.bbox
fields.notes: Page fractions [x0, y0, x1, y1], origin top-left, each 0..1, with 0 <= x0 < x1 <= 1 and the same in y. Unit-free, so there is no page_dims and none is wanted. A null bbox means on-this-page-no-box. Several boxes are UNIONED into one outline.

fields.name: row.evidence_ref.note

values: no page dimensions: the geometry could not be made unit-free, so no box is claimed
bbox lies outside the page, or has no area, so there is no box to draw
bbox extended past the page edge and was clamped

fields.notes: OPTIONAL and never null: the producer writes the key only when the note is truthy, and the schema types it string with pattern \S. The clamped wording still comes WITH a box; the other three come with a null bbox or a union. This is the per-row diagnostic -- a profile exporting evidence should carry it.

fields.name: header_edit.field
fields.notes: A steward may correct only these three. Their intersection with the four header review items the producer writes (pub_date, mfr, mfr_parent, doc_level_ltb_date) is {mfr} ALONE -- so a steward cannot correct an mfr_parent or a doc-level LTB date, and an export of steward-corrected header fields can only ever differ from extraction on mfr.

fields.name: header_edit.value
fields.notes: The corrected value.

fields.name: header_edit.reason
fields.notes: Why the steward changed it.

fields.name: header_edit.evidence_ref
fields.notes: The same EvidenceRef shape. A steward-supplied ref, not one doc-tools produced.

fields.name: row_edits.added
fields.notes: Rows the steward added. Defaults to [].

fields.name: row_edits.corrected
fields.notes: Rows the steward corrected. Defaults to [].

fields.name: row_edits.deleted
fields.notes: Rows the steward deleted. Defaults to [].

fields.name: row_edit_counts.header
fields.notes: How many header edits the correction carried -- bounded above by 3 by the header_edit.field enum.

fields.name: provenance.obtained_via
fields.notes: THE PROVENANCE RUNG the packet asks for. doc_tools/components/document_parser.py:32. None means this instance is a VETTED path and no provenance stamp is written at all -- so a null is not unknown-rung, it is no-stamp. NOT served on the extraction route, and NOT the same field as row.obtained_via.

fields.name: provenance.authoritative_source
fields.notes: ADR-0041 sibling of the rung. Default user-upload. Not served.

fields.name: provenance.standing
fields.notes: ADR-0041 standing, the trust rung at write time. Default unverified. Not served.

review_json_only.why_not_served: Not in ExtractionRow. It is the discriminator for whether a field gets a wire_evidence_ref at all (derived gets none), so its effect is visible on the wire even though it is not.
The internal fraction list; evidence_ref.bbox serves the single box, or the union of them.
Hardcoded to pending by the producer and never updated there -- review.json is an ingest OUTPUT, not a review store. An export must take approval from the promotion, never from this key.
A merge-added flag, not a BAML field. The same fact reaches the wire as obtained_via: inherited_doc_level.
